1.1 Graph of Quadratic Function Using Factors

blocks.prompt:
1 The graph of \(y = 3(x + 2)(x - 4)\) cuts the x-axis at:
(\(y = 3(x + 2)(x - 4)\) ka graph x-axis ko kahan kaatta hai?)

book_ref.quote: The graph will cut the x-axis at

blocks.prompt:
2 The vertex of the parabola \(y = (x + 1)(x - 5)\) is:
(Parabola \(y = (x + 1)(x - 5)\) ka vertex (chotti) kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Vertex \(x = \frac{-1 + 5}{2} = 2\) par hai; \(y = (3)(-3) = -9\). Is liye vertex \((2, -9)\).

book_ref.quote: represents the vertex of the parabola

blocks.prompt:
3 The y-intercept of \(y = -2(x - 3)(x + 1)\) is:
(\(y = -2(x - 3)(x + 1)\) ka y-intercept kya hai?)

book_ref.quote: the graph will cut the y-axis at

4 For \(y = -5(x - 1)(x - 4)\), as \(x \to -\infty\) and as \(x \to +\infty\):
(\(y = -5(x - 1)(x - 4)\) ke liye jab \(x \to -\infty\) aur \(x \to +\infty\):)
blocks.explanation: Bade \(|x|\) par dono factors ka sign aik jaisa hota hai, product positive; \(a = -5 < 0\) se negative. Is liye dono taraf \(y \to -\infty\) (neeche khulta hai).

book_ref.quote: This statement means the graph behaves the same way on both ends

options.text: x-axis ko \((3, 0)\) aur \((-3, 0)\) par kaatta hai
x-axis ko vertex \((3, 0)\) par chhoota hai

blocks.explanation: Dohraya hua factor \((x - 3)^{2}\) sirf aik x-intercept \(x = 3\) deta hai jahan graph sirf chhoota hai; \((3, 0)\) vertex hai.

book_ref.quote: The graph touches the x-axis at

blocks.prompt:

(\(y = 2(x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3)\) ke liye jab \(x \to -\infty\):)
blocks.explanation: Bohat baayen teenon factors negative hain; teen negatives ka product negative, aur \(a = 2 > 0\) sign nahi badalta. Is liye \(y \to -\infty\).

book_ref.quote: then what will be the behaviour of

7 After factorizing, the vertex of \(y = x^{2} - 6x + 8\) is:
(Factorize karne ke baad \(y = x^{2} - 6x + 8\) ka vertex kya hai?)

book_ref.quote: Suppose, after factorizing

blocks.prompt:

blocks.explanation: \(3x - 2 = 3\left(x - \frac{2}{3}\right)\), is liye \(a = 3\) aur roots \(\frac{2}{3}\) aur \(-1\) hain.

blocks.text: 1.2 Predicting a Quadratic Function from its Graph

blocks.prompt:
9 A parabola has x-intercepts \(2\) and \(5\) and passes through \((0, 20)\). In \(y = a(x - 2)(x - 5)\), \(a\) equals:
(Parabola ke x-intercepts \(2\) aur \(5\) hain aur yeh \((0, 20)\) se guzarta hai. \(y = a(x - 2)(x - 5)\) mein \(a\) kitna hai?)

book_ref.quote: To find \(a\), substitute the coordinates of a third known point into the equation.

blocks.prompt:
10 A parabola touches the x-axis at \(x = 3\) and passes through \((0, -18)\). Its equation is:
(Parabola x-axis ko \(x = 3\) par chhoota hai aur \((0, -18)\) se guzarta hai. Is ki equation (muadla) kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Chhoona yani dohraya factor: \(y = a(x - 3)^{2}\). Phir \(-18 = 9a\), \(a = -2\).

book_ref.quote: If the graph only touches the x-axis at

11 The x-intercepts \(x = h\) and \(x = k\) of a parabola fix its equation \(y = a(x - h)(x - k)\) except for:
(Parabola ke x-intercepts \(x = h\) aur \(x = k\) is ki equation \(y = a(x - h)(x - k)\) ko poora tay karte hain, siwaye:)
blocks.explanation: Har \(a(x - h)(x - k)\) ke intercepts same hain; sirf \(a\) (shakal aur simt) maloom nahi, teesra point use tay karta hai.

book_ref.quote: Here, \(a\) is a constant that determines the shape and direction of the parabola.

blocks.prompt:
12 The quadratic with x-intercepts \(-1\) and \(3\) passing through \((1, 8)\) is:
(Woh quadratic jis ke x-intercepts \(-1\) aur \(3\) hain aur jo \((1, 8)\) se guzarta hai:)

book_ref.quote: can be determined from its graph by using the factor form

blocks.prompt:
13 Which one of the following functions is algebraic?
(In mein se kaun sa function algebraic hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\sqrt[3]{x^{2} + 1}\) mein sirf jama, power aur root hai, is liye algebraic. Baaqi mein \(x\) exponent, log ya trigonometric function ke andar hai.

book_ref.quote: is algebraic if it is obtained from

blocks.prompt:
14 Which one of the following functions is transcendental?
(In mein se kaun sa function transcendental hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(5^{x}\) mein variable exponent hai, is liye transcendental; \(x^{5}\), \(\frac{1}{x^{2}+1}\), \(\sqrt{x}\) algebraic hain.

book_ref.quote: A function is called a transcendental function if it is not algebraic.

blocks.prompt:
15 The function \(y = \sqrt{x - 2}\) satisfies the polynomial equation:
(Function \(y = \sqrt{x - 2}\) kis polynomial equation ko satisfy karta hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(y = \sqrt{x - 2}\) ka square: \(y^{2} = x - 2\), yani \(y^{2} - (x - 2) = 0\). Is liye algebraic.

book_ref.quote: if it satisfies a polynomial equation of the form

blocks.prompt:
16 Which polynomial equation in \(y\) is satisfied by \(y = \dfrac{x}{x + 4}\), \(x \ne -4\)?
(\(y = \dfrac{x}{x + 4}\), \(x \ne -4\) kis polynomial equation ko satisfy karta hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(x + 4\) se zarb dein: \((x + 4)y - x = 0\); coefficients polynomials hain.

book_ref.quote: where each \(P_{i}(x)\) is a polynomial in \(x\)

blocks.prompt:
17 Which one of the following is a fundamental transcendental function?
(In mein se kaun sa fundamental transcendental function hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\cos^{-1} x\) khud \(x\) ka standard inverse trigonometric function hai. Baaqi mein composition, jama ya zarb hai.

book_ref.quote: Fundamental transcendental functions are the commonly used standard transcendental functions

blocks.prompt:
18 For which value of \(a\) is \(y = a^{x}\) an exponential function?
(\(a\) ki kis qeemat par \(y = a^{x}\) exponential function hai?)
blocks.explanation: Base ke liye \(a > 0\), \(a \ne 1\) zaroori. \(1^{x}\) constant hai, \(0^{x}\) \(x \le 0\) par undefined, \((-3)^{1/2}\) real nahi.

book_ref.quote: Why the conditions \(a > 0\) and \(a \ne 1\) on \(y = a^{x}\)?

blocks.prompt:
19 Which one of the following is a non-fundamental transcendental function?
(In mein se kaun sa non-fundamental transcendental function hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(e^{x^{3}}\) composition hai (exponent \(x^{3}\)). \(9^{x/2} = 3^{x}\) fundamental hai, \(\ln x\) aur \(\tan^{-1} x\) bhi.

book_ref.quote: or by applying transformations and composition, are non-fundamental transcendental functions

blocks.prompt:
20 The function \(y = 2^{3x}\) can be written as the standard function:
(Function \(y = 2^{3x}\) ko kis standard function ki shakal mein likha ja sakta hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(2^{3x} = (2^{3})^{x} = 8^{x}\), is liye fundamental hai.

book_ref.quote: is a standard transcental function, because, it can be written as

blocks.prompt:
21 The function \(y = x\cos x\) is:
(Function \(y = x\cos x\) kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(x\cos x\) algebraic \(x\) aur standard \(\cos x\) ka product hai: transcendental magar non-fundamental.

book_ref.quote: are examples of functions which are not fundamental transcendental functions

blocks.prompt:
22 In \(e = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n!}\), the sum of the first four terms (\(n = 0, 1, 2, 3\)) is:
(\(e = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n!}\) mein pehle chaar terms (\(n = 0, 1, 2, 3\)) ka majmua kya hai?)

book_ref.quote: is called the natural exponential function, where

blocks.prompt:
23 Which function represents exponential decay?
(Kaun sa function exponential decay (kami) dikhata hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(0 < a < 1\) decay deta hai; sirf \(\frac{3}{4}\) 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan hai.

book_ref.quote: represents exponential decay

blocks.prompt:
24 \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x}\) is equal to:
(\(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x}\) kis ke barabar hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\left(\frac{1}{a}\right)^{x} = a^{-x}\), is liye \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x} = 3^{-x}\).

book_ref.quote: The number \(a\) is called the base of the exponential function.

blocks.prompt:
25 \(f(x) = a^{x}\), \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), is an exponential function when:
(\(f(x) = a^{x}\), \(x \in \mathbb{R}\) kab exponential function hai?)
blocks.explanation: Definition mein base positive aur 1 ke ilawa hona chahiye; 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan base bhi jaiz hai (decay).

book_ref.quote: is called an exponential function

blocks.prompt:
26 Which point lies on the graph of \(y = 4^{x}\)?
(Kaun sa point \(y = 4^{x}\) ke graph par hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(4^{-2} = \frac{1}{16}\) aur \(4^{2} = 16\), is liye \(\left(-2, \frac{1}{16}\right)\) graph par hai.

book_ref.quote: Make a short table of values

blocks.prompt:
27 The range of \(y = 5^{x}\) is:
(\(y = 5^{x}\) ki range kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(5^{x} > 0\) hamesha, 0 ke qareeb bhi jata hai aur bohat bara bhi, is liye range \(]0, \infty[\) (0 kabhi nahi).

book_ref.quote: We conclude that the range of the exponential function (1) is

blocks.prompt:
28 The graph of \(y = \left(\frac{2}{7}\right)^{x}\) cuts the y-axis at:
(\(y = \left(\frac{2}{7}\right)^{x}\) ka graph y-axis ko kahan kaatta hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(x = 0\): \(\left(\frac{2}{7}\right)^{0} = 1\). Har exponential graph \((0, 1)\) se guzarta hai.

book_ref.quote: cuts the \(y\)-axis at the point \((0, 1)\)

blocks.prompt:
29 The horizontal asymptote of \(y = 4^{x}\) is:
(\(y = 4^{x}\) ka horizontal asymptote kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(x \to -\infty\) par \(4^{x} \to 0^{+}\), magar kabhi 0 nahi, is liye \(y = 0\) horizontal asymptote hai.

book_ref.quote: represents the horizontal asymptote for the exponential function

blocks.prompt:

(Function \(y = (0.3)^{x}\) kaisa hai?)
blocks.explanation: Base \(0.3\) 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan hai, is liye \(a^{x}\) poore domain par strictly decreasing hai.

book_ref.quote: is strictly decreasing when \(0 < a < 1\)

blocks.prompt:
31 As \(x \to -\infty\), \(3^{x}\) tends to:
(Jab \(x \to -\infty\), \(3^{x}\) kis taraf jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(a > 1\) ke liye \(\lim_{x \to -\infty} a^{x} = 0^{+}\): qeematein positive reh kar 0 ke qareeb jati hain.

book_ref.quote: is shown using the equation

blocks.prompt:
32 The value of \(27^{-2/3}\) is:
(\(27^{-2/3}\) ki qeemat kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(27^{-2/3} = \frac{1}{3^{2}} = \frac{1}{9}\). Negative exponent reciprocal deta hai, negative number nahi.

book_ref.quote: Since \(a > 0\), the product of positive numbers is positive.

blocks.prompt:

(\(3^{x}\) ke one-to-one hone se \(3^{x} = 81\) ka hal kya hai?)

book_ref.quote: is injective. It follows that any horizontal line meets the graph

blocks.prompt:

(Line \(y = c\) kab \(y = f(x)\) ka horizontal asymptote hai?)
blocks.explanation: Horizontal asymptote woh ufqi line \(y = c\) hai jis ke liye \(x \to \pm\infty\) par \(f(x) \to c\). (Kitab ka lafz 'vertical' ghalat chhapa hai.)

book_ref.quote: A horizontal asymptote is a horizontal line

blocks.prompt:
35 The function \(y = x^{2}\) is strictly increasing on:
(Function \(y = x^{2}\) kis interval par strictly increasing hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(0 < x_{1} < x_{2}\) ho to \(x_{1}^{2} < x_{2}^{2}\); \(]-\infty, 0[\) par yeh strictly decreasing hai.

book_ref.quote: This function is strictly decreasing on

blocks.prompt:
36 \(\sinh x\) is defined as:
(\(\sinh x\) ki definition kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\sinh\) mein farq \(e^{x} - e^{-x}\) taqseem 2; jama \(\cosh\) ka hai, quotient \(\tanh\) ka.

book_ref.quote: They are defined using combinations of

blocks.prompt:
37 The range of \(\cosh x\) is:
(\(\cosh x\) ki range kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\cosh x \ge 1\), \(\cosh 0 = 1\), aur dono taraf \(\infty\), is liye range \([1, \infty)\).

book_ref.quote: The hyperbolic functions are defined as follows:

blocks.prompt:
38 The domain of \(\coth x\) is:
(\(\coth x\) ka domain kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\coth x = \frac{\cosh x}{\sinh x}\), aur \(\sinh x = 0\) sirf \(x = 0\) par, is liye domain \(\mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\}\). \((-\infty, -1) \cup (1, \infty)\) is ki range hai.

book_ref.quote: so \(\coth\) and \(\operatorname{csch}\) (which divide by \(\sinh x\)) have domain

blocks.prompt:
39 The range of \(\operatorname{sech} x\) is:
(\(\operatorname{sech} x\) ki range kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\operatorname{sech} x = \frac{1}{\cosh x}\), \(\cosh x \ge 1\), is liye \((0, 1]\); 1 \(x = 0\) par milta hai.

book_ref.quote: so \(\operatorname{sech} x = 1/\cosh x\) lies in \((0, 1]\)

blocks.prompt:
40 The range of \(\tanh x\) is:
(\(\tanh x\) ki range kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\tanh x\) mein numerator ka size denominator se chhota hai, is liye \(-1 < \tanh x < 1\).

book_ref.quote: is always smaller in size than its denominator

blocks.prompt:
41 The point \((\cosh t, \sinh t)\) lies on the curve:
(Point \((\cosh t, \sinh t)\) kis curve par hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\cosh^{2} t - \sinh^{2} t = 1\), is liye yeh point hyperbola \(x^{2} - y^{2} = 1\) par hai.

book_ref.quote: satisfy the equation of the hyperbola

blocks.prompt:

blocks.prompt:
44 The value of \(\tanh(\ln 2)\) is:
(\(\tanh(\ln 2)\) ki qeemat kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\tanh(\ln 2) = \frac{3/2}{5/2} = \frac{3}{5}\) (yeh \((-1, 1)\) mein hona chahiye).

book_ref.quote: The other four are made from them exactly as in trigonometry

blocks.prompt:

(Kaun si identity har real \(x\) ke liye durust hai?)
blocks.explanation: Definitions rakhne se \(\cosh^{2} x - \sinh^{2} x = \frac{4}{4} = 1\): hyperbolic identity mein minus hai.

book_ref.quote: Writing \(\cosh^{2} x + \sinh^{2} x = 1\) by copying the trigonometric identity

blocks.prompt:

(Kaun sa point \(y = \sinh x\) aur \(y = x\) dono ke graph par hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\sinh 0 = 0\), is liye \((0, 0)\) dono par hai; \(\sinh 1 \approx 1.18\), 1 nahi.

book_ref.quote: so the graph of \(\sinh x\) passes through the point \((0, 0)\)

blocks.prompt:
47 The graph of \(y = \cosh x\) is symmetric about:
(\(y = \cosh x\) ka graph kis ke gird symmetric hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\cosh(-x) = \cosh x\): even function, \(y\)-axis ke gird symmetric.

blocks.prompt:

blocks.explanation: \(\sinh(-x) = \frac{e^{-x} - e^{x}}{2} = -\sinh x\) (odd function).

book_ref.quote: Such a function is called odd, and its graph is symmetric about the origin

blocks.prompt:

blocks.explanation: 1 se ooper har height \(x\) aur \(-x\) dono par milti hai, horizontal line graph ko do dafa milti hai: one-to-one nahi.

blocks.explanation: \(\cosh x\) ka restricted domain \([0, \infty)\) \(\cosh^{-1} x\) ki range banta hai; \(\cosh^{-1} 1 = 0\) shamil hai.

blocks.prompt:

blocks.explanation: \(\frac{x + 1}{x - 1} > 0\) sirf jab \(|x| > 1\); yeh \(\coth x\) ki range bhi hai.

blocks.prompt:

blocks.explanation: \(\sqrt{\frac{16}{9} + 1} = \frac{5}{3}\), is liye \(\ln\left(\frac{4}{3} + \frac{5}{3}\right) = \ln 3\).
